requirements.quote: Client and Server implementations using TLS [RFC5246] should provide capabilities to ensure that any SSL certificates provided when initiating a TLS [RFC5246] connection are associated with the hostname of the Client connecting or Server being connected to.
requirements.condition: When a TLS-using Client validates the Server certificate presented while initiating a connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide a capability to verify that the certificate is associated with the hostname of the Server being connected to.
requirements.why_checkable: Certificates with matching and mismatching Server hostnames can be presented and validation outcomes observed.

requirements.quote: Client and Server implementations using TLS [RFC5246] should provide capabilities to ensure that any SSL certificates provided when initiating a TLS [RFC5246] connection are associated with the hostname of the Client connecting or Server being connected to.
requirements.condition: When a TLS-using Server validates a Client certificate presented while initiating a connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide a capability to verify that the certificate is associated with the hostname of the connecting Client.
requirements.why_checkable: Certificates with matching and mismatching Client hostnames can be presented and validation outcomes observed.

requirements.quote: Client and Server implementations using TLS [RFC5246] can choose to provide capabilities to check Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs [RFC5280]) and Online Certificate Status Protocol (OSCP) [RFC6960] to prevent revoked certificates from being used.
requirements.condition: When evaluating whether a TLS implementation supplies CRL and OSCP certificate-status checking capabilities.
requirements.required_behavior: Check certificate revocation status and prevent revoked certificates from being used.
requirements.why_checkable: The capability is explicitly optional, so its absence cannot produce a deterministic conformance failure.

requirements.quote: Server implementations might disconnect Clients that breach its security rules.
requirements.condition: When a Client breaches a Server's security rules.
requirements.required_behavior: Disconnect the Client.
requirements.why_checkable: The statement only says the Server might disconnect and does not require that response, so a deterministic pass/fail test is unavailable.

requirements.quote: If Client or Server SSL certificates are lost or it is considered that they might be compromised they should be revoked (utilizing CRLs [RFC5280] and/or OSCP [RFC6960]).
requirements.condition: When a Client or Server SSL certificate is lost.
requirements.required_behavior: Revoke the certificate using CRLs and/or OSCP.
requirements.why_checkable: The certificate's revocation status can be queried after the loss event.

requirements.quote: If Client or Server SSL certificates are lost or it is considered that they might be compromised they should be revoked (utilizing CRLs [RFC5280] and/or OSCP [RFC6960]).
requirements.condition: When a Client or Server SSL certificate is considered potentially compromised.
requirements.required_behavior: Revoke the certificate using CRLs and/or OSCP.
requirements.why_checkable: The certificate's revocation status can be queried after it is marked potentially compromised.

requirements.quote: Client or Server authentication credentials, such as User Name and Password, that are lost or considered compromised should be revoked and/or reissued.
requirements.condition: When Client or Server authentication credentials are lost.
requirements.required_behavior: Revoke and/or reissue the credentials.
requirements.why_checkable: Authentication with the old credentials and any replacement credentials can be tested after the loss event.

requirements.quote: Client or Server authentication credentials, such as User Name and Password, that are lost or considered compromised should be revoked and/or reissued.
requirements.condition: When Client or Server authentication credentials are considered compromised.
requirements.required_behavior: Revoke and/or reissue the credentials.
requirements.why_checkable: Authentication with the old credentials and any replacement credentials can be tested after the compromise decision.

requirements.quote: Client and Server implementations using TLS [RFC5246] should allow for session renegotiation to establish new cryptographic parameters (replace session keys, change cipher suites, change authentication credentials).
requirements.condition: During a long-lasting TLS connection when new session keys are needed.
requirements.required_behavior: Allow TLS session renegotiation to replace the session keys.
requirements.why_checkable: A renegotiation can be initiated and the resulting session keys compared with the prior keys.

requirements.quote: Client and Server implementations using TLS [RFC5246] should allow for session renegotiation to establish new cryptographic parameters (replace session keys, change cipher suites, change authentication credentials).
requirements.condition: During a long-lasting TLS connection when the cipher suite is to be changed.
requirements.required_behavior: Allow TLS session renegotiation to change cipher suites.
requirements.why_checkable: A renegotiation can request a different mutually supported cipher suite and the negotiated result can be inspected.

requirements.quote: Client and Server implementations using TLS [RFC5246] should allow for session renegotiation to establish new cryptographic parameters (replace session keys, change cipher suites, change authentication credentials).
requirements.condition: During a long-lasting TLS connection when authentication credentials are to be changed.
requirements.required_behavior: Allow TLS session renegotiation to change authentication credentials.
requirements.why_checkable: A renegotiation using new credentials can be initiated and the authenticated identity or credential observed.

requirements.quote: Servers may disconnect Clients and require them to re-authenticate with new credentials.
requirements.condition: When evaluating credential refresh behavior for a long-lasting connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Disconnect the Client and require re-authentication using new credentials.
requirements.error_behavior: Terminate the existing connection before re-authentication.
requirements.why_checkable: The behavior is permitted but not required, so failure to exercise it cannot establish noncompliance.

requirements.quote: Where implementations choose to use SOCKS, they should support both anonymous and user-name password authenticating SOCKS proxies.
requirements.condition: When an MQTT implementation chooses to use SOCKS.
requirements.required_behavior: Support anonymous SOCKS proxies.
requirements.why_checkable: An anonymous SOCKS proxy can be configured and outbound MQTT connection establishment tested.

requirements.quote: Where implementations choose to use SOCKS, they should support both anonymous and user-name password authenticating SOCKS proxies.
requirements.condition: When an MQTT implementation chooses to use SOCKS.
requirements.required_behavior: Support SOCKS proxies that authenticate with a user name and password.
requirements.why_checkable: A username/password-authenticating SOCKS proxy can be configured and outbound MQTT connection establishment tested.

requirements.quote: In the latter case, implementations should be aware that SOCKS authentication might occur in plain-text and so should avoid using the same credentials for connection to a MQTT Server.
requirements.condition: When an implementation uses username/password SOCKS authentication that might transmit credentials in plain text.
requirements.required_behavior: Use credentials distinct from those used to connect to the MQTT Server.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse the MQTT Server credentials for SOCKS authentication.
requirements.why_checkable: Configured SOCKS and MQTT credential identifiers can be compared for equality.

requirements.quote: When using the clear communication profile, the MQTT protocol runs over an open network with no additional secure communication mechanisms in place.
requirements.condition: When an implementation or deployment claims the clear communication profile.
requirements.required_behavior: Run MQTT over an open network.
requirements.why_checkable: The term open network is not defined with observable minimum properties in this chunk, so this profile characteristic lacks a standalone pass/fail criterion.

requirements.quote: When using the clear communication profile, the MQTT protocol runs over an open network with no additional secure communication mechanisms in place.
requirements.condition: When an implementation or deployment claims the clear communication profile.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Add a secure communication mechanism to that profile.
requirements.why_checkable: The connection stack can be inspected for TLS, tunnels, or other added secure communication mechanisms.

requirements.quote: When using the secured network communication profile, the MQTT protocol runs over a physical or virtual network which has security controls e.g., VPNs or physically secure network.
requirements.condition: When an implementation or deployment claims the secured network communication profile.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a physical or virtual network with security controls.
requirements.why_checkable: The statement gives only non-exhaustive examples and no minimum security-control properties, so a standalone pass/fail criterion is incomplete.

requirements.quote: When using the secured transport profile, the MQTT protocol runs over a physical or virtual network and using TLS [RFC5246] which provides authentication, integrity and privacy.
requirements.condition: When an implementation or deployment claims the secured transport profile.
requirements.required_behavior: Transport MQTT using TLS.
requirements.why_checkable: The transport handshake and record layer can be observed to verify TLS use.

requirements.quote: When using the secured transport profile, the MQTT protocol runs over a physical or virtual network and using TLS [RFC5246] which provides authentication, integrity and privacy.
requirements.condition: When an implementation or deployment claims the secured transport profile.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide authentication through its TLS transport.
requirements.why_checkable: The TLS handshake can be inspected to verify authenticated peer identity according to the configured mode.

requirements.quote: When using the secured transport profile, the MQTT protocol runs over a physical or virtual network and using TLS [RFC5246] which provides authentication, integrity and privacy.
requirements.condition: When an implementation or deployment claims the secured transport profile.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide integrity protection through its TLS transport.
requirements.why_checkable: Tampered TLS records can be injected and rejection observed.

requirements.quote: When using the secured transport profile, the MQTT protocol runs over a physical or virtual network and using TLS [RFC5246] which provides authentication, integrity and privacy.
requirements.condition: When an implementation or deployment claims the secured transport profile.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide privacy through its TLS transport.
requirements.why_checkable: Network capture can verify that MQTT Control Packet content is not exposed as plaintext.

requirements.quote: TLS [RFC5246] Client authentication can be used in addition to – or in place of – MQTT Client authentication as provided by the Username and Password fields.
requirements.condition: When evaluating whether TLS Client authentication is supported alongside or instead of MQTT Username/Password authentication.
requirements.required_behavior: Allow TLS Client authentication as an additional or replacement authentication mode.
requirements.why_checkable: The sentence permits these modes but does not require an implementation to support either configuration, so absence cannot establish noncompliance.

requirements.quote: MQTT Control Packets MUST be sent in WebSocket binary data frames.
requirements.condition: When MQTT is transported over a WebSocket connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Send every MQTT Control Packet in WebSocket binary data frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send an MQTT Control Packet in a non-binary WebSocket data frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The WebSocket opcode of frames carrying MQTT bytes can be inspected.

requirements.quote: If any other type of data frame is received the recipient MUST close the Network Connection [MQTT-6.0.0-1].
requirements.condition: When an MQTT-over-WebSocket recipient receives a non-binary WebSocket data frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the Network Connection.
requirements.error_behavior: Terminate the Network Connection instead of continuing MQTT processing on it.
requirements.why_checkable: A text or other non-binary data frame can be injected and connection closure observed.

requirements.quote: A single WebSocket data frame can contain multiple or partial MQTT Control Packets. The receiver MUST NOT assume that MQTT Control Packets are aligned on WebSocket frame boundaries [MQTT-6.0.0-2].
requirements.condition: When one WebSocket binary data frame contains multiple complete MQTT Control Packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Parse and process every contained MQTT Control Packet independently of the single frame boundary.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assume the frame contains exactly one MQTT Control Packet.
requirements.why_checkable: Multiple complete Control Packets can be concatenated into one frame and all resulting protocol actions observed.

requirements.quote: A single WebSocket data frame can contain multiple or partial MQTT Control Packets. The receiver MUST NOT assume that MQTT Control Packets are aligned on WebSocket frame boundaries [MQTT-6.0.0-2].
requirements.condition: When an MQTT Control Packet is split across WebSocket binary data frame boundaries.
requirements.required_behavior: Reassemble and parse the Control Packet independently of the frame boundaries.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assume each frame boundary is also an MQTT Control Packet boundary.
requirements.why_checkable: A valid Control Packet can be divided across frames at arbitrary byte offsets and its processing observed.

requirements.quote: The client MUST include “mqtt” in the list of WebSocket Sub Protocols it offers [MQTT-6.0.0-3].
requirements.condition: When an MQTT Client offers WebSocket Sub Protocols while establishing its WebSocket connection.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the exact subprotocol name “mqtt” in the offered list.
requirements.why_checkable: The WebSocket opening handshake's offered subprotocol list can be inspected.

requirements.quote: The WebSocket Sub Protocol name selected and returned by the server MUST be “mqtt” [MQTT-6.0.0-4].
requirements.condition: When a Server accepts MQTT transport over WebSocket and selects a WebSocket Sub Protocol.
requirements.required_behavior: Select and return the exact subprotocol name “mqtt”.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected subprotocol in the WebSocket opening response can be inspected exactly.

requirements.quote: The WebSocket URI used to connect the client and server has no impact on the MQTT protocol.
requirements.condition: When MQTT-over-WebSocket connections use different valid WebSocket URIs.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep MQTT protocol parsing and behavior invariant with respect to the chosen WebSocket URI.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Alter MQTT protocol semantics based solely on the WebSocket URI.
requirements.why_checkable: Equivalent MQTT exchanges over different URIs can be compared for protocol-level behavior.
